gameConfig.failState: Run ends with a jumpscare if (a) a bad guest is still inside when the night ends, or (b) a deadly guest is accepted. No hearts, one life only.

mistakeRules.acceptBadGuest: Not fatal yet. The guest stays in the monitor and can still be kicked before the night ends.
mistakeRules.rejectGoodGuest: No death. Motel loses revenue (counted as 'Turned away' on the results screen).
mistakeRules.kickGoodGuest: No death. Motel loses revenue and the guest is counted as 'Wrongly kicked'.
mistakeRules.acceptDeadlyGuest: Instant death with jumpscare. Cannot be kicked.

rng.night2AnomalyMinimum: max(3, 6 - goodGuestsNotYetUsed). Only 6 good guests exist, so this keeps night 2 from running out.

schemaNotes.idMatchesVisible: true = ID card agrees with the 'visible' traits. false = at least one mismatch (see idInfo vs visible).
schemaNotes.tellType: How a disguised guest can be caught: idMismatch | dialogue | nightLog | glitch | none
schemaNotes.ifAdmittedNotKicked: Consequence at the end of the night if the player lets this guest in and never kicks them. The game is one life only.
schemaNotes.specialEffect: Optional. Extra behavior triggered by a guest, such as audio played when they are accepted.
schemaNotes.killsPlayer: true = instant death and jumpscare the moment they are accepted.
schemaNotes.difficulty: 1 = easy to spot, 2 = needs questions, 3 = only the night log gives it away
schemaNotes.commandmentLink: Which idol or virtue the guest represents (First and Second Commandments theme). Shown on the results screen.

anomaly.name: Belz

specialEffect.note: Quiet whispering in the background for the rest of the night. Stops if Belz is kicked.

dialogue.askDetails: You should know me. Everyone knows me. This place is practically mine.
dialogue.askId: Do you really need to check? Fine.

nightLog: Belz never entered the room

anomaly.tell: Claims to be a regular, but the guest book has no record of him. The 'What you see' header text glitches while he is on screen. The log shows he never entered his room.
anomaly.disguise: Everything on his ID matches what you see.

commandmentLink.name: Pride
commandmentLink.meaning: Making yourself the center and treating yourself like a god

anomaly.ifAdmittedNotKicked: Game over (jumpscare) when the night ends

dialogue.greeting: Good evening! I'll pay double. Triple, if you skip the paperwork.
dialogue.askDetails: Money is no problem. Name your price. Everyone has one, don't they?
dialogue.askId: Do we really need that? I can make it worth your while.

anomaly.tell: Mentions money before anything else and tries to bribe you to skip the ID check. Directly ties to the theme: MONEY.

anomaly.ifAdmittedNotKicked: Game over (jumpscare) when the night ends. Motel also loses money

dialogue.greeting: Peace be with you. Open the door. I am the one you have been waiting for.
dialogue.askDetails: Why do you ask? Just believe me and let me in. Do not test me.
dialogue.askId: I need no ID. But since you ask... it says exactly what I tell it to.

anomaly.tell: Demands to be trusted without any questions. The ID looks self-written and 'verified' by himself. The glow around his face flickers. He is angry when tested.
anomaly.disguise: Radiant, calm and perfectly matching his ID.

commandmentLink.name: False Christ
commandmentLink.meaning: A false savior. Scripture warns against false christs and false prophets (Matthew 24:24)

dialogue.greeting: What a lovely place. I have visited many homes, and yours is special. May I come in?
dialogue.askDetails: I know what you want. I know what everyone wants. Let me help you.
dialogue.askId: Here. Every detail is perfect, as you can see.

anomaly.tell: Everything about him is too perfect. The age on his ID reads 0. His shadow is missing from the guest screen. Text on the screen glitches into other words.
anomaly.disguise: An angel of light who says everything the player wants to hear.

commandmentLink.name: The Deceiver
commandmentLink.meaning: Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14)
